sub_units.name: Data Sufficiency
sub_units.content: Data Sufficiency problems test the ability to determine whether given data is sufficient to answer a question, without necessarily solving it. This topic covers analyzing one or two statements independently and together, identifying redundant information, and making logical judgments about data adequacy. It is a unique reasoning format widely used in competitive exams like CAT and GMAT.

sub_units.name: Decision Making
sub_units.content: Decision Making problems present real-life scenarios requiring logical evaluation of given conditions to arrive at the best course of action. This topic covers analyzing multiple criteria, prioritizing conditions, handling conflicting constraints, and selecting optimal decisions. It tests practical reasoning skills and is commonly featured in management aptitude exams.

sub_units.name: Critical Reasoning
sub_units.content: Critical Reasoning involves evaluating arguments by identifying their structure, assumptions, strengths, and weaknesses. This topic covers strengthening and weakening arguments, identifying flaws in reasoning, drawing inferences, and evaluating conclusions. It develops the ability to think clearly and logically about complex issues.

sub_units.name: Logical Deduction
sub_units.content: Logical Deduction requires deriving valid conclusions from given premises using formal rules of logic. This topic covers if-then statements, contrapositive reasoning, chain logic, and multi-conditional deductions. It builds the ability to follow logical chains accurately and is fundamental to all areas of analytical reasoning.

sub_units.name: Pattern Recognition
sub_units.content: Pattern Recognition involves identifying underlying patterns in sequences of numbers, letters, figures, or symbols. This topic covers number series, letter series, figure series, and analogy-based patterns. Strong pattern recognition skills enable quick identification of rules and trends, which is essential for solving reasoning and data interpretation problems.

sub_units.name: Venn Diagrams
sub_units.content: Venn Diagrams use overlapping circles to visually represent relationships between different groups or sets. This topic covers two-set, three-set, and multi-set problems, finding intersections and unions, and solving word problems using Venn diagram logic. It is a powerful tool for solving problems related to classification, grouping, and logical relationships.

sub_units.name: Ranking Problems
sub_units.content: Ranking Problems involve determining the position or rank of a person or object in a sequence based on given conditions. This topic covers linear ranking, comparison-based ranking, and problems involving ties and missing data. It tests the ability to organize information logically and deduce positions from partial data.

sub_units.name: Calendar Problems
sub_units.content: Calendar Problems involve determining the day of the week for a given date, counting odd days, and understanding leap year rules. This topic covers finding days for past and future dates, calculating the number of days between two dates, and solving problems involving recurring events. It combines arithmetic skills with logical pattern application.

sub_units.name: Clock Problems
sub_units.content: Clock Problems deal with the relationship between the hour and minute hands of a clock. This topic covers calculating angles between hands, finding times when hands overlap or are opposite, and solving problems involving gains and losses of time. Understanding the relative speed of clock hands is key to mastering these problems.

sub_units.name: Cube & Dice Problems
sub_units.content: Cube and Dice Problems involve spatial reasoning about three-dimensional objects. This topic covers painted cube problems, dice orientation and opposite faces, unfolded cube patterns, and cutting and reassembly problems. It tests the ability to visualize 3D objects from 2D representations and apply logical rules to spatial configurations.
